record.paper_title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
record.original_question: Let Dhat(n) be the largest quantity such that every n-point set P in the plane contains a point p in P with at least Dhat(n) distinct distances to the other points of P. Determine the asymptotic order of Dhat(n).

evidence.quote: simple upper bound is ˆD(n) ≤ D(n) = O(n/ √ log n). However, Guth and Katz’s bound does not immediately imply a m atching lower bound for ˆD(n). The current best lower bound, obtained by Katz and Tardos [ 33], is ˆD(n) = Ω(n(48− 14e)/ (55− 16e)) ≈ Ω(n0. 864). Problem 36. Find the asymptotic value of ˆD(n). Given a planar point set P and a point p ∈ P , we denote by ˆDp(P) the number of distinct distances between p and the other points of P. We set ˆDΣ(P) = ∑ p∈P ˆDp(P) and ˆDΣ(n) = min |P|=n ˆDΣ(P). It is not hard to verify that when P is a √ n × √ n section of Z2, we have ˆDΣ(P) = Θ ( n2/ √ log n ) . This implies that ˆDΣ(n) = O ( n2/ √ log n ) , which Erd˝ os conjectured [20, 22]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and a point $p\in P$, let $\hat D_p(P)$ denote the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\|:q\in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm. Define
$$\hat D(n)\;=\;\min_{\substack{P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\\|P|=n}}\;\max_{p\in P}\;\hat D_p(P),$$
so that $\hat D(n)$ is the largest quantity with the property that every $n$-point planar set contains some point having at least $\hat D(n)$ distinct distances to the remaining points. Determine the asymptotic order of $\hat D(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.

Known facts: the trivial upper bound from the Guth–Katz theorem gives $\hat D(n)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, and the best known lower bound is $\hat D(n)=\Omega\!\left(n^{(48-14e)/(55-16e)}\right)\approx \Omega(n^{0.864})$.
artifact.status_search_result: The pinned distinct distances problem remains open. The Guth–Katz solution (2010) settled the unpinned Erdős distinct distances problem, giving $D(n)=\Omega(n/\log n)$, but the matching lower bound for $\hat D(n)$ was not implied. The best known lower bound is still the Katz–Tardos bound $\hat D(n)=\Omega(n^{0.864\ldots})$, while the upper bound is $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$. Subsequent works on bisectors and pinned distances have improved related quantities but have not closed the gap.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent work investigates pinned distances via bisector incidences without closing the gap to n/√log n.
